thread:
Maya: Quick idea — introduce a compact routing expression for tenant policies so console presets + advanced lines can coexist.
Samir: curious, do you mean a tiny DSL or a compressed JSON shape?
Maya: mini-DSL. Example sketch: ```priority = if plan == "enterprise" then 100 elif plan == "pro" then 50 else 10; fallback = [{variant:"rwd-4b",weight:0.8},{variant:"rwd-2b-quant",weight:0.2}]; soft_quota_ms = 200```
Lisa: neat — compact for power users. but how will we validate/preview in console?
Toni: Console UX: offer three presets (free/pro/enterprise) and an "advanced expression" toggle. presets map to compiled policy. :thumbsup:
pm-ethan: Product note — we need clear semantics for soft vs hard quota and telemetry hooks for fallback_count / eviction_rate / avg_cost_per_token.
Samir: API debate: do we accept DSL in the API or only canonical JSON? accepting DSL increases surface area and parsing burden.
Alex: prefer accepting both but compile to canonical JSON on write. keeps runtime simple and lets us evolve DSL.
Maya: compile-on-apply then store canonical. runtime reads canonical only.
Samir: ok but we need deterministic compilation and schema migration story.
Lisa: validation UI should show live-compiled JSON and sample request simulation (region, plan, seq_len) with which variant would be selected.
Toni: +1. Also a "why-this-route" explain button for debugging.
Maya: enforcement model: soft_quota = allow but prefer cheaper variants / mark metric; hard_quota = reject with 429 or route to best-effort fallback depending on tenant_policy.hard_action.
Samir: propose hard_action options: reject | fallback | degrade. fallback should be able to pick a variant table with weights and an optional latency_budget_ms.
pm-ethan: product would like default hard_action for free to be fallback->degrade to smallest quantized model, for enterprise default = reject.
Alex: metrics required: per-tenant p50/p95 latency, fallback_rate, quota_hits, cost_per_request, tokens_saved_by_cache. Also need combinational alerting: if fallback_rate spikes + p95 increases = route regression.
Maya: rollout UX: allow canary by percent of tenants or by "plan==pro && region==eu-west-1" selector. and auto-revert if regression thresholds hit.
Samir: technical: evaluation must be cheap at request-time — compiled rules should be O(1) lookups + tiny predicate checks. no regex per-request.
Lisa: console should show impact estimates when editing policy (expected cost delta, likely fallback_rate) — can be based on sampled logs.
Toni: question about model variants lifecycle: need version pinning and automatic compatibility check when variant set changes. e.g. if rwd-4b loses kv-cache feature, we must not route queries expecting long context.
Alex: agree. include capability metadata on variant objects and compile-time validation against tenant requirements (max_seq, funcs_used).
Maya: edge-case: multi-tenant customers with subteams that want different policies. allow policy inheritance with overrides. keep UI simple: visual inheritance tree.
Samir: also consider quotas by window (per-min, per-day) + token vs request quotas. compact expr should expose both.
pm-ethan: timeline ask: prototype API + compiler in 2 sprints, console integration + presets in sprint 4.
Lisa: I'll draft UX flows and wireframes.
Maya: I'll open a small RFC describing DSL grammar, compile rules, and canonical JSON shape.
Alex: I'll stub runtime compile endpoint and sample compiled schema.
Samir: I'll own validation + migration story.
Toni: ping me for console preview tests.
devops-bot: deploy-checklist created: infra/routing-policy-compiler PR required, runtime feature flag, console feature flag.
Maya: cool. action items above. keeping this thread for RFC comments.
Samir: +1. thanks everyone.
